1.explanation:
To fully reproduce and debug this issue you need:
• architecture.md          – overview of Lighthouse’s pipeline and where trace-processor fits in
• configuration.md         – how Lighthouse configures trace categories (to ensure FrameCommittedInBrowser is captured)
• understanding-results.md – how raw trace events map to audit data (context for FrameCommittedInBrowser and threads)
• error-reporting.md       – details on this specific "Unable to determine tid" error and troubleshooting tips
• puppeteer.md             – example of running Lighthouse via Puppeteer/Node (same environment as the user)
• recipes/custom-gatherer-puppeteer/readme.md – concrete code showing how to collect a DevTools timeline trace with Puppeteer so you can inspect the failing trace and iterate on the trace-processor fix
1.bug_scenario:
When Lighthouse is run (via Node) against the Treo.sh site with default trace categories, the DevTools timeline emits a FrameCommittedInBrowser event carrying a processPseudoId (instead of processId). The trace-processor’s findMainFramePidTids() function filters for that event, then calls .map(e => e.args.data.processId) (leaving undefined in the pid array).  Because no valid pid is found, the subsequent search for a "CrRendererMain" thread entry returns no tid and throws the error "Unable to determine tid for renderer process."  In the paused debugger snapshot you can see:
  • frameCommittedEvts[0].args.data.processPseudoId is set, but processId is missing
  • mainFramePids ends up [undefined]
  • pidToTid map remains empty and triggers the error throw
